summary: This program walks through a fixed list of student names, asks whether each one is present, and collects the names of anyone who does not answer "yes" so it can print them at the end.

lines.text: A list holds several values in one variable, in the order you wrote them. This is the fixed roll to be called.
An empty list is created before the loop starts so there is somewhere to put names as they are discovered. Starting empty is the normal pattern when you are building a collection up as you go.
The for loop hands the block below one name at a time, storing it in the variable student, until the list runs out.
The f-string drops the current name straight into the question, and .lower() converts the reply to lowercase so that "Yes", "YES", and "yes" are all treated the same.
The != operator means "is not equal to", so anything other than a yes counts as absent. Treating only "yes" as present means a blank or mistyped answer errs on the side of marking the student absent.
append adds the name to the end of the absentees list, which is how the list grows during the loop.
This sits outside the loop, at the left margin, so it runs once after every student has been asked.
